sections.readerQuestion: With Pogačar out injured, what did the 2026 men's Worlds course in Montréal demand and who was placed to win it, and how did the race actually go?
sections.usefulAnswer: Explains why Pogačar was absent (Vuelta crash, season ended 5 September), the 273.4km course (12 laps of 13.4km, 269m per lap, Camillien-Houde 2.3km at 6.2%), the spread of contenders, and the result: McNulty's solo from a flat section 32km out, winning by 13 seconds. Ends with a club-rider lesson about attacking where the group relaxes.
sections.evidence: Six claims each cite a named source (Cyclingnews 5 and 25 and 27 September 2026, UCI course release March 2026). All seven external citation URLs returned HTTP 200 on 22 October 2026. relatedPosts slugs and in-body links resolve to existing content files. Rendered at 1280x800 and 375x812 on the dev server: h1, four body H2s, claims, resources, key quote, FAQ and Read the Guide sections present.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish. Changed only the sponsor boilerplate from "coaching program" to "coaching programme" for British English. No YouTube ID: the episode was not in the channel feed, so the page shows audio platform links only.

sections.readerQuestion: What made the 2026 women's Worlds road race hard to call, and how did Vollering win it?
sections.usefulAnswer: Course (180.1km, eight laps, 2,570m), the home-favourite pressure on Vallières, the contenders, then the result: the crash 95km out that ended Vallières's race, Vollering's attack at 38.5km, being caught at 15km and still winning the two-up sprint. Closes with the point that counting your remaining efforts is a skill, not fitness.
sections.evidence: Five cited claims with sources (Cyclingnews 24, 26 and 27 September 2026; UCI course release). External URLs returned 200. Companion blog and men's preview links resolve. Rendered desktop and mobile: no overflow, no broken images, FAQ and claims sections present.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish. Sponsor boilerplate changed to "programme". No YouTube ID available in the channel feed.

sections.readerQuestion: Which of my regular rides return the most fitness for the hour, once I count the recovery they cost?
sections.usefulAnswer: Sets out the fitness-per-hour test (what it builds, what it costs, who controls the dose), explains why social and fasted rides score lower, cites Seiler's intensity-distribution work and the Rønnestad and Appelhans interval trials, and gives a three-question exercise for the reader's last seven days. Does not invent a league table; points to the episode for the ranking.
sections.evidence: Four claims with sources including PubMed IDs 16430681, 24382021 and 40328438; PubMed returned HTTP 429 rate limiting to the link checker but the IDs match the cited papers. Eight relatedPosts and all in-body links resolve. YouTube ID cocruIsv69A added after matching the channel feed entry dated 21 September 2026 titled "The Best & Worst Cycling Sessions To Get Faster"; the thumbnail shows the ranked-tier graphic. Rendered desktop and mobile with the video embed present.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish with the YouTube embed added and "programme" spelling.

sections.readerQuestion: What did the Court of Arbitration for Sport actually decide about Contador's clenbuterol positive, and why does it still divide people?
sections.usefulAnswer: Walks through the 50 pg/mL finding, the strict-liability burden of proof, why the meat explanation failed on evidence, why CAS also rated the transfusion theory unlikely, the contaminated-supplement conclusion, the sanction and the 2021 WADA rule change. Each step is tied to the award or contemporaneous reporting.
sections.evidence: Six claims cite the CAS award, Cyclingnews, Cycling Weekly, The Inner Ring, CBS/AP and the WADA 2021 stakeholder notice. The original arbitrationlaw.com award PDF link returned HTTP 404, so it was replaced with the Wayback Machine copy of the CAS jurisprudence database PDF (snapshot 21 January 2022); I opened that PDF and confirmed it is the award of 6 February 2012 in CAS 2011/A/2384 and 2386. The award's facts section (pages 4 and 5) supports the sample date, time, laboratory and concentration and the examining judge, acquittal and appeal sequence; the claim sources now cite the facts section instead of invented paragraph numbers. YouTube ID MaWO089sRZc matched to the feed entry dated 25 September 2026 (thumbnail reads "Contador: the case doesn't add up"). Rendered desktop and mobile with the video embed.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish with the corrected award citation, the YouTube embed and "programme" spelling.

sections.readerQuestion: Which VO2 max interval format is best, and why do the same intervals work for one rider and not another?
sections.usefulAnswer: Summarises the Seiler 2013, Rønnestad 2015 and Appelhans 2025 findings, explains that pacing and how intensity is controlled change the answer, treats the 4.6%-in-four-weeks block with stated caution, and gives a repeatable rule: one format, even pacing, four to six weeks.
sections.evidence: Five claims cite PubMed 21812820, 24382021, 40328438 and 42237396 plus the episode description. relatedPosts and relatedEpisodes resolve. Rendered desktop and mobile: no overflow, claims and FAQ sections present. Not in the YouTube channel feed, so no video embed.
sections.editorialDecision: Publish. Only change since commit: "programme" spelling in the sponsor boilerplate.

claimsAndSources: Read every claim, citedClaim, citation and reviewedSource in the thirteen files. Every external citation URL in the seven 22 October files was HEAD-checked on 22 October 2026: all returned 200 or 202 except PubMed and drinkag1.com (HTTP 429 rate limiting, IDs and paths match the cited records) and the arbitrationlaw.com CAS award PDF (404), which was replaced with the Wayback Machine copy of the CAS jurisprudence PDF after opening it and confirming it is the 6 February 2012 award. Two claim sources that cited paragraph numbers the award does not use now cite its facts section. The PubMed IDs in the 12 October files match the papers named. Race facts match the Cyclingnews reports cited. No product claims.
examplesAndReasoning: The sessions pieces give the scoring questions, a fix per session and a reader exercise rather than an invented league table. The Worlds blog ties each of five lessons to a specific race moment with times and distances. The Contador pages explain the burden of proof before the verdict. The strength and VO2 pieces state the limits of the evidence (low-certainty meta-analysis, small trials, crossover design). No invented sets, loads or results.
voiceAndCuts: Read all thirteen pages in full. British English throughout; the only US spellings were "program" in the shared sponsor paragraph of seven episodes, changed to "programme", and "Optimize" inside a quoted paper title, left as the title. No banned slop terms found (grep for the Roadman banned list returned only that paper title). The "and and" typo in the indoor upgrades episode was fixed. "Last weekend" in the Worlds blog became "on the last weekend of September". Nothing else cut.
